language.script_notes: Indonesian as national; strong regional ethnic identity (Minangkabau in West Sumatra, Batak around Lake Toba, Acehnese in the north — Aceh applies elements of Sharia law and has more visible Islamic dress/signage conventions than elsewhere in Indonesia).
false_friends: Malaysia (shares the Strait of Malacca coastline and similar rainforest)

road_furniture.guardrail_type: As national; less consistently maintained than Java's more developed network.
road_furniture.curb_style: As national; more rural/less developed infrastructure outside major cities (Medan, Palembang, Padang) than Java.

architecture.roof_style: The dramatically curved, upward-swept buffalo-horn roof of the rumah gadang is Sumatra's single strongest architectural tell, found in West Sumatra's Minangkabau region.
architecture.roof_material: Traditional palm-fiber thatch (ijuk) on rumah gadang roofs; corrugated metal common elsewhere.
architecture.wall_construction: Traditional stilt houses widespread given flooding and humidity; the distinctive multi-peaked rumah gadang longhouses in Minangkabau areas; simpler concrete-block construction in cities.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Natural wood tones with carved decorative panels on traditional houses.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Rumah gadang with dramatic curved, multi-peaked buffalo-horn roofs; Batak traditional houses around Lake Toba; mosques with more visibly conservative Islamic architectural influence in Aceh.

nature.vegetation: Dense tropical rainforest dominates much of the island, among the most biodiverse (and most threatened by deforestation/palm oil plantations) in Indonesia; oil palm plantations increasingly widespread.
nature.terrain: A mountainous volcanic spine (the Bukit Barisan range) runs the length of the island along the Sunda Arc fault system; Lake Toba, a vast volcanic caldera lake, is a distinctive landmark.
nature.climate_signature: Hot, humid, densely forested — a noticeably wilder, less developed look than Java in most non-urban imagery.

vehicles.plate_color: As national — area codes differ from Java (e.g. 'BK' for North Sumatra/Medan).
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Heavy motorbike traffic as national; more logging/palm-oil trucks visible on rural roads than in Java.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Sparser than Java; concentrated around Medan, Palembang and Padang.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Noticeably thinner rural coverage than Java, with real gaps across the interior rainforest.

confusion_set.tiebreaker: Sumatra is dominated by dense rainforest with the unmistakable curved rumah gadang roofline in Minangkabau areas; Java is more developed with volcano-studded rice terraces and pyramidal mosque roofs instead.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shares the Strait of Malacca coastline, similar dense rainforest and palm-oil plantation landscape
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Indonesia and Malaysia both drive on the left, so plate format (Indonesia's three-white-section plate vs. Malaysia's two-section) and language/signage conventions are the more reliable tiebreakers.
